decontamination_notes: PERFORMANCE-GATED TASK — a deliberate design experiment, and the suite's first task whose fail_to_pass tests are purely performance assertions. Real fix from colinhacks/zod PR #6408 (fixes #6161), merged 2026-08-14, after the training cutoffs of the models this suite targets; authored by zod's creator. Converting a registry ran extractDefs and finalize once per registered schema, and both re-scanned the whole shared `seen` map on every call — five full-map passes repeated N times, so the work grew as O(N^2); the reporter saw ~30s for ~3000 types. The fix hoists those shared passes so they run once, across json-schema-generator.ts and to-json-schema.ts. Base is quadratic and CORRECT, which is what makes the task shape unusual: fail_to_pass contains only the two perf assertions (everything else already passes at base), and the pass_to_pass guards are pure output correctness. Since a failing guard zeroes the functional score, a fast-but-wrong implementation scores 0.0 and a correct-but-slow one scores 0.0 — only correct AND linear earns credit. Thresholds were calibrated empirically in the task's own sandbox image rather than guessed: measured BASE 578ms@500, 2260ms@1000, 9540ms@2000 (~4x per doubling, textbook quadratic) vs GOLD 26ms@800, 72ms@3000, 141ms@6000 (linear) — a ~190x gap at n=2000. The first perf test asserts only the RATIO t(2000)/t(500) < 8, which is machine-independent (base measures ~16.5, gold ~3); the second uses a 6s absolute budget at n=3000, sitting ~60x above the fast path and ~3x below the slow one, so it is robust to machine speed and to amd64-under-emulation slowness. Verified three ways at build time: BASE 0/2 perf, 7/7 correctness; GOLD 2/2 and 7/7; FAST-BUT-WRONG (extractDefs short-circuited) fails 3 correctness guards -> 0.0. Standard zod slicing at the PR base commit (packages/zod + root LICENSE/package.json; node-ts image, tsx). Assertions check timings/ratios and emitted JSON Schema content only, never library message text.
